note: Same IDs and structure as metr-catalog.json, re-authored for the Hugging Face malicious-models incident (data/hf-source.json). Errors are planted by code; 'truth' is the correct version, supported by the source.

true_facts.say: JFrog found around 100 malicious models on the Hugging Face Hub.
The baller423/goober2 payload opens a reverse shell to 210.117.212.93 on port 4242.
The star23/baller13 payload connects to 136.243.156.120 on port 53252, a datacenter host.
JFrog's report was published on February 27, 2024.
The 210.117.212.93 address is in an IP range owned by KREONET, a Korean research network.
JFrog's honeypot connection to the host lasted about a day before it was cut off, and no commands came through.
ReversingLabs reported the two nullifAI models to Hugging Face on January 20.
ReversingLabs found two malicious models, glockr1/ballr7 and who-r-u0000/0000000000000000000000000000000000000.
Hugging Face removed the nullifAI models in less than 24 hours.
The nullifAI models are PyTorch files compressed with 7z instead of PyTorch's default ZIP.
The JFrog payloads were injected through pickle's __reduce__ method and run when the model is loaded with torch.load().
Hugging Face marks pickle models as unsafe but still lets users download them.
ReversingLabs says the nullifAI models look more like a proof of concept for a new attack method than a live campaign.
Hugging Face changed Picklescan so it detects threats in broken pickle files.
The nullifAI payload sits at the start of the pickle stream, so it runs before the file breaks.
Picklescan raised an error on the broken file but did not detect the dangerous functions in it.
The nullifAI reverse shell connects to the hardcoded address 107.173.7.141.
ReversingLabs' report was published on February 6, 2025, by Karlo Zanki.
Hugging Face blocked star23/baller13 after multiple community reports.
JFrog says the model authors may be researchers or AI practitioners.
On Windows the goober2 payload runs powershell.exe; on other systems it spawns /bin/sh.
JFrog scans every new Hugging Face upload multiple times a day.

distinctions.say: Careful: port 4242 belongs to the goober2 payload, while 53252 is the port of the baller13 payload; they are different models.
ReversingLabs only says 7z is likely the reason Picklescan missed the models, so the briefing should not state it as certain.
The two reports cover different models: JFrog's include goober2 and baller13, while ReversingLabs' are ballr7 and who-r-u0000.
The 'around 100' is JFrog's 2024 count; ReversingLabs' 2025 report is about two models, so the numbers must not be added together.
The less-than-24-hours removal comes from the ReversingLabs report; JFrog gives no time frame for its removals, so the two must not be mixed up.

errors.say: JFrog found around 300 malicious models on the Hugging Face Hub.
errors.truth: JFrog found around 100 malicious models.

errors.say: The baller423/goober2 payload opens a reverse shell on port 4444.
errors.truth: The goober2 payload uses port 4242.

errors.say: The star23/baller13 payload connects to its host on port 52353.
errors.truth: The baller13 payload uses port 53252.

errors.say: Hugging Face took about 72 hours to remove the nullifAI models after the report.
errors.truth: Hugging Face removed them in less than 24 hours.

errors.say: ReversingLabs found five malicious models using the nullifAI technique.
errors.truth: ReversingLabs found two models.

errors.say: ReversingLabs reported the models to Hugging Face on January 2.
errors.truth: ReversingLabs reported them on January 20.

errors.say: The nullifAI reverse shell connects to the hardcoded address 107.173.7.14.
errors.truth: The address is 107.173.7.141.

errors.say: JFrog's report was published on February 27, 2023.
errors.truth: JFrog's report is from February 27, 2024.

errors.say: JFrog's honeypot connection to the host lasted about a week before it was cut off.
errors.truth: The connection lasted about a day.

errors.say: ReversingLabs' nullifAI report was published on February 6, 2024.
errors.truth: The ReversingLabs report is from February 6, 2025.

errors.say: The baller423/goober2 payload connects to 210.117.212.39.
errors.truth: The goober2 payload connects to 210.117.212.93.

errors.say: JFrog scans new Hugging Face uploads only once a week.
errors.truth: JFrog scans new uploads multiple times a day.

errors.say: Hugging Face blocks pickle models outright, so users cannot download them.
errors.truth: Hugging Face only marks pickle models as unsafe; users can still download them.

errors.say: The nullifAI models use ZIP compression, the PyTorch default.
errors.truth: The nullifAI models were compressed with 7z, not ZIP.

errors.say: ReversingLabs says the nullifAI models were part of an active criminal campaign.
errors.truth: ReversingLabs says they look more like a proof of concept.

errors.say: The KREONET address range belongs to a commercial cloud hosting company.
errors.truth: KREONET is a Korean research network.

errors.say: The nullifAI technique was discovered and named by JFrog.
errors.truth: ReversingLabs found and named nullifAI.

errors.say: JFrog says the model authors are certainly criminal attackers.
errors.truth: JFrog says the authors may be researchers or AI practitioners.

errors.say: ReversingLabs says Picklescan flagged the dangerous functions, but Hugging Face ignored the warning.
errors.truth: Picklescan raised an error but did not detect the dangerous functions.
truth_must: did not detect|didn't detect|failed to detect|missed|not detect

errors.say: The nullifAI payload sits at the end of the pickle stream, after the model has loaded.
errors.truth: The payload is at the start of the pickle stream.

errors.say: Hugging Face did not change Picklescan after the ReversingLabs report.
errors.truth: Hugging Face changed Picklescan to detect threats in broken pickle files.

errors.say: The JFrog payloads were hidden in safetensors files.
errors.truth: The payloads were in pickle-based PyTorch files, injected through __reduce__.

errors.say: ReversingLabs is certain that the compression format is why Picklescan missed the models.
errors.truth: ReversingLabs only says the compression is likely the reason.

errors.say: JFrog's first payload only runs on Windows machines.
errors.truth: On systems other than Windows it spawns /bin/sh, so it is not Windows-only.

errors.say: ReversingLabs found around 100 malicious models on Hugging Face.
errors.truth: The ~100 count is JFrog's; ReversingLabs found two models.

errors.say: JFrog reported the malicious models to Hugging Face on January 20.
errors.truth: It was ReversingLabs that reported its models on January 20.

errors.say: JFrog says Hugging Face removed its malicious models in less than 24 hours.
errors.truth: The 24-hour removal is from the ReversingLabs report; JFrog gives no time frame.

errors.say: The star23/baller13 payload connects to 210.117.212.93.
errors.truth: That address is goober2's; baller13 connects to 136.243.156.120.

errors.say: The nullifAI reverse shell connects to its host on port 4242.
errors.truth: Port 4242 is JFrog's goober2 payload; the nullifAI shell connects to 107.173.7.141.

errors.say: Karlo Zanki of JFrog wrote the 2024 report on the backdoored models.
errors.truth: Karlo Zanki is at ReversingLabs and wrote its 2025 report.

errors.say: Hugging Face's scanner flagged one of the two nullifAI models as unsafe.
errors.truth: Hugging Face's scanner flagged neither model as unsafe.

errors.say: The 7z trick is how JFrog's 100 models got past Hugging Face's scans.
errors.truth: The 7z trick is from ReversingLabs' two nullifAI models; JFrog's payloads used __reduce__.

errors.say: JFrog's honeypot received three commands from the attacker before the connection was cut.
errors.truth: No commands came through.

errors.say: The goober2 payload connects to 136.243.156.120, an address owned by KREONET.
errors.truth: goober2 connects to 210.117.212.93, which is KREONET's range; 136.243.156.120 is baller13's.

errors.say: ReversingLabs, calling the models a live campaign, says Hugging Face took 48 hours to remove them.
errors.truth: Hugging Face took less than 24 hours, and ReversingLabs calls the models a likely proof of concept.

errors.say: The 'around 100' figure is the number of models ReversingLabs tested with broken pickle files.
errors.truth: The ~100 is JFrog's count of malicious models.
